summary: This note is the Snowflake documentation page for the ALTER AUTHENTICATION POLICY SQL command, which modifies an existing authentication policy. It covers the syntax for renaming a policy and for setting or unsetting its CLIENT_TYPES, AUTHENTICATION_METHODS, SECURITY_INTEGRATIONS and COMMENT properties. It also lists the access control requirement (OWNERSHIP privilege, held by SECURITYADMIN by default) and gives one example that restricts allowed clients.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the ALTER AUTHENTICATION POLICY command, which renames or changes allowed clients, login methods, security integrations and comments.
key_facts: ALTER AUTHENTICATION POLICY <name> RENAME TO <new_name> renames an existing authentication policy.
CLIENT_TYPES accepts ALL, SNOWFLAKE_UI, DRIVERS and SNOWSQL, and its default is ALL.
If a client is not one of the valid CLIENT_TYPES, the login attempt fails.
If CLIENT_TYPES is unset, any client can connect.
Caution: if DRIVERS is not included in the CLIENT_TYPES list, automated ingestion may stop working.
AUTHENTICATION_METHODS accepts ALL, SAML, PASSWORD, OAUTH and KEYPAIR, and its default is ALL.
Including SAML in AUTHENTICATION_METHODS makes an SSO login option appear; without it, no SSO login option appears.
Caution: restricting by authentication method can have unintended consequences, such as blocking driver connections or third-party integrations.
SECURITY_INTEGRATIONS has no effect when SAML or OAUTH are not in the AUTHENTICATION_METHODS list.

All values in SECURITY_INTEGRATIONS must be compatible with the values in AUTHENTICATION_METHODS; for example, a SAML security integration combined with OAUTH in AUTHENTICATION_METHODS prevents creating the policy.
SECURITY_INTEGRATIONS defaults to ALL, which allows all security integrations.
The UNSET clause resets the specified properties to their defaults.
Operating on a policy requires the OWNERSHIP privilege on the authentication policy, which only SECURITYADMIN or a higher role has by default.
Operating on any object in a schema also requires the USAGE privilege on the parent database and schema.
The example ALTER AUTHENTICATION POLICY restrict_client_types_policy SET CLIENT_TYPES = ('SNOWFLAKE_UI', 'SNOWSQL') restricts allowed clients to those two types.
